To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the image context, which is the textual content of the Web pages containing an image, is a rich source of semantic information that can be used to characterize the image content, (2) the image context can be used to bridge the semantic gap between the low-level representation of an image in terms of colors and textures, and its semantic interpretation, (3) image understanding can be improved by using the image context, (4) the image context is heterogeneous, noisy, and inconsistent, and

the contextual information of Web pages is a valuable resource for image indexing and retrieval, but its quality is unpredictable and that the state-of-the-art in image understanding is not yet able to fully leverage this information.

(i) the image contextual information of a Web image is the set of textual components of the Web page containing the image, (ii) the image contextual components can be classified into three types: (i) image title, (ii) image caption, (iii) image description, and (iii) the most relevant image contextual components are the image title, image caption and image description, (iv) the most relevant textual component of an image is its image title,
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following topics: (a) the identification and the extraction of the relevant contextual information, (b) its semantic characterization and (c) its exploitation to improve image retrieval.
bridging the semantic gap between Web images and their contextual information in the framework of image retrieval.
the characterization and exploitation of contextual information of Web-based image content.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, although the contextual information of Web pages can be exploited in order to characterize the image content, it still remains a major challenge to automatically characterize the Web image content using contextual Web information.

the state of the art in Web image understanding has reached a stage where the research is mature enough to be applied to large-scale real world applications, but that the research community is still lacking a unified framework that would allow for a systematic comparison of existing approaches and for the identification of the key issues and the most promising directions for future work.
the Web has been the main source of information for image understanding and the state-of-the-art is still far from being able to fully exploit it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided an extensive review of the current state-of-the-art of the Web image understanding field and identified the major research issues.

we have identified a set of problems that need to be tackled in order to leverage on Web images’ contextual information for image understanding, and we have reviewed the existing literature to highlight the most relevant solutions.
we have provided the state-of-the-art in Web image understanding and have identified the most relevant research directions for the near future.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the contextual information of Web pages is a valuable resource to characterize Web images, however, it requires further investigation to fully leverage on it.
the Web provides rich and diverse sources of information for image understanding.
the Web provides rich information for characterizing image content and understanding its semantics.
